div.head: II Cn 31.2
div.ab: Gyf him seo lad berste, gylde þam cingce his were; ⁊ si se man utlah.
Gif him seo lad berste, gilde þam cyninge his were; ⁊ sy se man utlage.
Si purgatio frangat ei, soluat regi weram suam; et qui fugit, extra legem habeatur.
[Gyf him seo lad berste, gylde þam cingce his were] ⁊ beo se man utlah wið ðone cyng.
Gyf him seo lad berste, gylde þam cingce his were; and si se man utlah.
[And if he fails to clear himself, he shall pay his (own) wergeld to the king], and the man shall be an outlaw towards the king.
If the exoneration fails, he is to pay a fine equal to his wergild to the king, and the fugitive is to be declared an outlaw.
And if the exculpation fails, he is to pay his [own] wergild to the king and the man is to be an outlaw.
Wenn ihm diese Reinigung misslingt, zahle er dem König sein Wergeld. Und jener Untergebene sei friedlos (gegenüber dem König B).
If this clearing fails him, let him pay the king his wergild. And let that man be an outlaw (with respect to the king, B).
div.note: B skips a line here. Liebermann compares I Atr 1.13.
utlah: B adds wið ðone cyng
